newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Belgians leave eastern Zaire town for evacuation.
newsitem.headline: Belgians leave eastern Zaire town for evacuation.

text.p: About 15 Belgians and other foreigners left the eastern Zairean town of Bukavu on Monday in a road convoy escorted by Zairean troops to be evacuated by plane, witnesses said.

They said the foreigners, including children clutching teddy bears, were escorted by Zairean troops to Bukavu airport, about 50 km (30 miles) north of the city, which most foreign aid workers left on Saturday because of worsening security.
"We have a flight from Bukavu today. The destination is Entebbe (in Uganda)," a Belgian Foreign Ministry spokesman said in Brussels.
"The convoy has arrived at Bukavu airport and they have been protected by a military escort," he said.
He could not confirm whether 15 Belgians were among the foreigners.
Evacuees said they expected to leave aboard a 34-seat Fokker plane, flying in from the city of Goma to the north of Bukavu.
Banyamulenge Tutsi rebels advanced last week close to Bukavu and fearful Zairean troops have looted aid agency vehicles and robbed foreigners and Zairean civilians in the lakeside city.
Belgium issued a fresh call on Sunday for its nationals living in eastern Zaire to leave.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman in Brussels said the Belgian embassy in Kinshasa had individually contacted the 230 Belgians remaining in the two war-ravaged provinces of North and South Kivu.
